A1.justification: Both PDFs describe QuEST and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Matching retained material across their substantial reorganization supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V3 reports original quantization experiments on LSUN, ImageNet, and Stable Diffusion, together with component ablations, activation analyses, and generated examples.

after.justification: V4 retains original generation and quantization results and adds CIFAR10 experiments, further baseline comparisons, and full-finetuning comparisons.

M1.justification: V3 uses timestep-dependent activation scales and groups neighboring timesteps through a dedicated temporal quantizer. V4 instead explicitly uses one parameter set across timesteps, removing that component from the formulation. Selective temporal and attention-layer finetuning with local and global supervision remains.

E1.justification: V4 adds low-resolution CIFAR10 generation evaluation in Appendix 7, Table 11. The existing LSUN-Bedrooms, LSUN-Churches, ImageNet, and COCO-prompt Stable Diffusion coverage remains.

E2.justification: V4 adds TFMQ-DM comparisons on Bedrooms and ImageNet in Table 9 and a full-finetuning comparator in Table 8. Figure 4 also adds EfficientDM to the qualitative comparison. The main benchmark comparator sets otherwise remain.

E3.justification: V4 introduces a full-finetuning control matched to QuEST's 2.2k training iterations and adds sFID/IS evaluation for Bedrooms in Table 10. Existing main evaluation samplers and sample counts remain. V4 describes token corruption as random noise in the main text but zeroing in the appendix, leaving that setting uncertain.

E4.justification: V3's timestep-sampling frequency sweep and Figure 5 are removed. V4 adds selective-versus-full-finetuning efficiency and performance analysis in Table 8. Temporal-embedding, loss-component, activation-distribution, and token-corruption analyses remain; the precomputed-embedding discussion reuses Table 2.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. V4's reimplementation/rerun annotations provide provenance without introducing repeated-trial uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Important reported rankings change. In Table 3, EfficientDM's W8A8 Bedrooms/Churches FIDs of 2.98/4.01 become generation failures. In Table 4, QuEST's W4A8 IS changes from 346.02 to 354.97, while EfficientDM's W4A4 sFID/IS change from 7.75/250.90 to 9.28/199.96. V4 also adds Tables 8–11 results and reverses QALoRA's reported 5.62 FID decrease to an increase. Identical baseline implementations across versions are not established.

T1.justification: V4's main theorem replaces the full-precision output surrogate in v3's residual expressions with the ground-truth target and adds an argument for neglecting the second-order term within an acceptable bound. The core proposition and appendix's telescoping Taylor derivation remain essentially unchanged.

C1.justification: V4 drops v3's standalone time-aware quantizer contribution and its claim to first generate readable W4A4 Stable Diffusion images. The theoretical sufficiency claim becomes feasibility support with an explicit disclaimer of a method guarantee. Efficient, data-free selective finetuning and state-of-the-art performance remain central claims.

C2.justification: V4 expands the explanation of why precomputed temporal embeddings can be incompatible with the quantized network and how global supervision addresses this. It qualifies the theoretical argument and adds discussion of full-finetuning memory limits for Stable Diffusion. The appendix's limitations and broader-impact paragraph is retained.

D1.justification: V4 identifies the component baseline as AdaRound, marks reimplemented/rerun results, and supplies iteration counts and resource measurements for the new finetuning comparison. It omits v3's 20-epochs-per-timestep statement and explicit higher-precision exceptions for boundary layers and attention products. The code link has the same destination.

R1.justification: V4 repositions QuEST from an extension of the PTQ framework into a separate parameter-efficient finetuning category and explicitly acknowledges prior temporal-preservation work. It adds TFMQ-DM, Temporal Dynamic Quantization, BitsFusion, PTQ4DiT, QLoRA, and other relevant work, while removing several generic references and narrowing the novelty claims.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and method narrative are extensively rewritten. Related work moves into the main text; three properties become one challenge plus two properties; alignment components receive separate subsections; theory follows the method; and ablations receive a dedicated discussion subsection.

P2.justification: V4 adopts a two-column layout, redraws Figure 1, revises Figure 2 annotations, restructures tables and appendix image grids, and replaces Figure 4's comparison panel. It removes the sampling-frequency figure and adds Tables 8–11. Retained appendix illustrations are rearranged.

improvement.justification: Clearer organization, narrower theoretical and priority claims, and the added full-finetuning control and TFMQ-DM/CIFAR10 comparisons provide a limited overall quality gain. Missing training and precision details, insufficient explanations for major baseline-score replacements, and conflicting token-corruption descriptions limit reproducibility and the strength of that improvement.
